content.title: About
content.content: Caesar dressing is a classic salad dressing created in the 1920s at Caesar's restaurant in Tijuana, Mexico. Core ingredients include egg yolk, olive oil, anchovies, Parmesan cheese, garlic, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, and mustard. The dressing has a creamy texture, bright tangy‑salty flavor, and a subtle heat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The original recipe was invented by Italian immigrant Caesar Cardini, who worked in his father's restaurant.
Traditional preparation emulsifies the yolk and oil, requiring vigorous whisking.
Authentic versions used whole anchovies, but many modern recipes substitute anchovy paste or omit it entirely.
Caesar dressing is most often served with romaine lettuce, croutons, and Parmesan, but it also works as a dip for vegetables and seafood.
In the United States, Caesar dressing ranks among the top three salad dressings after ranch and vinaigrette.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Egg yolk and Parmesan provide vitamin B12 and riboflavin, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Olive oil supplies monounsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Garlic and lemon juice are high in antioxidants that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Calcium and protein
items.content: Hard cheese adds calcium and high‑quality protein beneficial for bones and muscles.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: Some recipes include fermented Worcestershire sauce, which may aid gut microbiota.

items.title: Egg and dairy allergy
items.content: The dressing contains egg yolk and cheese, which can trigger reactions in allergic individuals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Worcestershire sauce and anchovies make the dressing salty; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Raw eggs can harbor salmonella; use pasteurized eggs or a ready‑made mayo base to reduce risk.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Olive oil and cheese add calories; moderate the amount if you are managing weight.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Traditionally, Caesar dressing is tossed with romaine lettuce, croutons, and Parmesan, often topped with grilled chicken. It also works as a dip for vegetable sticks, seafood, or as a spread for sandwiches and pasta salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dressing in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5‑7 days. For longer storage, freeze in small portions; shake or stir well before use as ingredients may separate.
